sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 18-02-2023 at about 7.30 p.m., the petitioner and his friend were proceeding on the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK-5932, to go from Bengaluru to Shivagange.

When they reached Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 road, near Makli Sky Walk,
Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time the rider of said motorcycle rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner,
endangering the human life and suddenly applied the front brake.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner and rider both fell down and the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Abhay Vasista Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

Earlier to the accident he was working as an agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to file his written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-KK-5932 and its liability, subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it is contended that, the person driving the vehicle has 'no relation in force' as on the date of accident to drive the vehicle.
Further it is contended that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-KK-5932 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, as on the date of accident.

The respondent No.1/owner of said vehicle knowingly entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, in violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.

Hence, there is a willful breach of terms and conditions of the Gangadhara N vs Srinivas Murthy C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48105962/
2 policy by the owner of the insured vehicle and hence this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation and the petition against it is liable to be dismissed.

Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

Further it is contended that, the insured vehicle is not at all involved in any accident and it was falsely implicated in the alleged accident, in collusion with the owner, rider and other authorities, in order to get unlawful benefit from the insurance company.
Further it is contended that, immediately after the accident no complaint was lodged before the police and there is an inordinate delay in lodging the complaint.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: 9. Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 18-02-2023 at about 7.30 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK-5932 as a pillion rider, on Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 road, near Makli Sky Walk, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk,
Bengaluru, at that time his friend, who was the rider of said motorcycle, rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and suddenly applied the front brake.

Due to the said impact,
the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident he was working as agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.5 is true copy of reply to notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act,
Ex.P.6 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.7 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.9 is discharge summary, Ex.P.10 are medical bills (total 46),

Ex.P.11 is notarized copy of Aadhar card of petitioner and Ex.P.12 is notarized copy of PAN card of petitioner.
11.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding and suddenly applying the brake by the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK- 5932.
Due to said impact, the petitioner being the pillion rider of the said motorcycle has fell down on the road and sustained grievous on his head.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8,
has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-5932.
12.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-5932 in the accident, the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to file his written statement and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and has taken specific defence that, the insured motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-5932 is not at all involved in the alleged accident and it is falsely implicated in the said accident, in collusion with the owner, rider and police authorities, in order to get unlawful benefit from the insurance company.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the said contentions.

Even,
the respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the right side of 30 feet wide Bengaluru-Tumkuru NH-48 road, near Makli Sky Walk, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru, due to suddenly applying the brake of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-5932.
Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.6 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.8 final report/charge- sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-KK-5932 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-5932.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate and Ex.P.9 discharge summary, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
He has suffered 1) right frontal extradural hemorrhage, 2) multiple facial bone fracture and 3) aspirational pneumonia.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 18-02-2023 at about 7.30 p.m., on Bengaluru-Tumkuru NH-48 road, near Makli Sky Walk, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-5932.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-5932 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained 1) right frontal extradural hemorrhage, 2) multiple facial bone fracture and 3) aspirational pneumonia.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. Towards loss of future income:
The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident he was working as agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor he has examined any doctor to establish that, due to injuries sustained in the accident he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to continue his avocation or perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his earning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
20. Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 46 medical bills, as per Ex.P.10.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.4,13,515/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,13,515/- under the head of medical expenses.
21. Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., 1) right frontal extradural hemorrhage, 2) multiple facial bone fracture and 3) aspirational pneumonia and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery.
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 10 days, from 18-02-2023 to 27-02-2023 in Abhay Vasishtha Hospital, Madanayakanahalli.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into consideration the injury sustained and the disability suffered by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Gangadhara N vs Srinivas Murthy C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48105962/
6 Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
22. Attendant charges:

sentences.text: As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 10 days in Abhay Vasishtha Hospital, Madanayakanahalli.
He might have spent some amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 10 =
Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
23. Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 10 days in Abhay Vasishtha Hospital, Madanayakanahalli.
He might have spent some amount for food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 10 =
Rs.8,000/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
24. Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Vidya Nagara, Obalapura, Chitradurga,
the accident has taken place on Bengaluru-Tumkuru NH-48 road, near Makli Sky Walk, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru and he has taken treatment at Abhay Vasishtha Hospital,
Madanayakanahalli.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the place of accident and the above hospital, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
25. Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.

Further,
he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do work and continue his avocation.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2023.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 10 days as in-patient at Abhay Vasishtha Hospital, Madanayakanahalli, for the grievous injuries caused to him.
He might have taken rest for about two months and lost his income for the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.16,000 x 2 = Rs.32,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
26. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 27 years and unfortunately he has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident and undergone treatment for 10 days as in-patient in Abhay Vasishtha Hospital,
Madanayakanahalli.
Further, it might have taken time of about two months for complete curing of the injuries suffered by him.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities during the treatment period would be just and reasonable.
27. Future medical expenses: The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that, he requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded under this particular head.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Nil 2.
Medical expenses Rs. 4,13,515-00 3. Pain and sufferings 60,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 10,000-00
5. Food and nourishment 8,000-00 6. Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 32,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 30,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses Nil
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,63,515/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
29. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-04-KK-5932.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the respondent No.1/rider of offending vehicle by name Srinivasamurthy S/o Chandranna was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA5220220011517 to drive the said vehicle and it is valid till 09-09-2038.
The policy issued by the respondent No.2 bearing No.140522223750080768, in respect of offending motorcycle, was valid from 05-10-2022 to 06-10-2023.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 18-02-2023.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-5932 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,63,515/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,63,515/- (Rupees five lakh sixty three thousand five hundred and fifteen only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment, on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

It has neither adduced any evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the said contentions.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,13,515/- under the head of medical expenses.
The accident has taken place in the year 2023.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities during the treatment period would be just and reasonable.
27. Future medical expenses: The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show that, he requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
